description:
FILED s539a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15, s542 resume) from the merge-review negative probes of the import-directive fact (#4881).  PRE-EXISTING (base = main code 24988e35 answers the same); not a regression of #4881.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3; scratch/s539a/rv/rv9.pl in the s539a worktree):
  use Test::More tests => 2;
  BEGIN { use_ok('constant', 'FOO', 5) }
  my @l = (FOO - 1, 7);
  is("@l", "4 7", 'FOO is a term');
perl: ok 1, ok 2 (use_ok runs `use constant FOO, 5` in main at BEGIN time, so FOO is a () constant for the rest of the parse).
PCL (base and tree): ok 1, not ok 2 -- got '5': FOO - 1, 7 is read as a call FOO(-1, 7) (a list operator swallowing the rest), a SILENT WRONG.

Why: the import-directive fact makes `use_ok('M', LIST)` in a BEGIN body `use M LIST` for the PARSE FACTS (prototypes, () constants, block-form arguments) through the module-facts merge; `constant` is not a module whose facts the merge reads -- `use constant NAME => V` is lowered by the compiler's own constant path, which never sees the directive.  Fix shape (rule 11): route the directive's `constant` case into the SAME constant-declaration path a literal `use constant` takes (one normalisation, no second copy), or document it as a limit.  Exotic in the wild (grep ~/.cpan/build for `use_ok(.constant.` before spending on it).
Related: rv3.pl / rv7b.pl / rv10.pl (a computed module name, a use_ok nested in an `if` in BEGIN, a user-defined use_ok without the marker) are the documented static limits of the mechanism (docs/shipped-modules.md "The import-directive fact"), same on the base; the #2610 detector stays silent on all of them = #4882.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611 -- after s543b's constants change) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- as filed: perl `ok 1 - use constant; / ok 2 - FOO is a term`, PCL `not ok 2` (got '5', expected '4 7').  The value is
  silently wrong; only the test row makes it visible.
LABEL: silent (subject now says so).
frequency_reason: `BEGIN { use_ok('constant', ...) }`: a test-file idiom (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: SILENT WRONG: BEGIN { use_ok('constant', NAME => V) } does not make NAME a () constant for the parse: `NAME - 1, 7` is read as a call FOO(-1, 7)
triage_reason: `BEGIN { use_ok('constant', ...) }` does not declare the constant for the parse
